transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-03
Time: 09:00 AM PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maeve Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (GreenField Eng Lead), Diego Morales (GreenField SRE), Priya Nair (Product), Samir (Data Ops)
Recording link: https://app.redwood.example/recording/ff-20270503-7b3f9a2e (placeholder)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
- Goal: scope POC harness integration and decide streaming vs non-streaming for GreenField's clinical summarization pipeline; align success criteria and timelines.
- Key asks: customer will provide canonical prompts + adversarial set; Redwood to run baseline non-streaming run and then streaming trials; security and networking checks to proceed in parallel.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maeve: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maeve from Redwood inference, today ravi and i will walk through the harness plan and get the success criteria nailed down. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Aisha: good, thanks, yes excited. quick note, we only have about 50 minutes so maybe focus on the benchmarks, scripts, and the streaming question.
[00:00:22] Ravi: sounds good. i put a short slide in the meeting notes but i'll just jump to the practicals — what scripts you have, how they're instrumented, and what your p99 goals look like.
[00:00:35] Diego: we mostly run a microservice that calls the model for patient-consent summarization, median payload size is about 1.4k tokens, but we have spikes up to 6k for concatenated history.
[00:00:47] Priya: and product wants <200ms p95 for interactive UI, but backend batch jobs can be more lenient. that's the tension.
[00:00:58] Ravi: okay that's helpful. so two workloads: interactive UI (low latency, smaller qps) and nightly batch processing (high throughput, can be non-streaming). correct?
[00:01:09] Aisha: exactly. we expect 120 rps baseline across regions for UI in peak, and the batch is roughly 200k calls overnight.
[00:01:21] Maeve: great. let's capture success criteria first, because that will drive the harness config. what would count as a successful POC?
[00:01:30] Priya: i'd say 3 things — 1) confirm p95 latency <250ms for UI in production-like env, 2) cost per thousand tokens meets our internal threshold (we gave a range in the questionnaire), and 3) no data exfil concerns — audit logs + KMS integration ok.
[00:01:47] Diego: and from SRE perspective, zero customer-visible errors during a sustained 10-minute window at peak qps. p99 under 1s is acceptable for UI if we can't hit p95.
[00:01:59] Samir: for accuracy we will run a small eval set — the adversarial prompts — to check regression vs our current model. not a production eval but sanity check.
[00:02:10] Ravi: noted. okay next, scripts: can you describe the harness scripts you currently have? are they HTTP-first, do they stream token by token, or do they buffer?
[00:02:22] Aisha: our devs created a prototype in-house — it uses a streaming websocket-like layer for the UI. the nightly jobs call a gRPC endpoint that expects the whole response before returning.
[00:02:36] Ravi: perfect example of mixed-mode. for the POC we usually recommend starting in non-streaming (whole response) mode to get stable latency and throughput numbers, then do targeted streaming runs to measure tail latency and client-side behavior.
[00:02:49] Maeve: and we can show the tradeoffs: streaming reduces perceived latency to first token but can increase resource pressure on the server at scale if many clients keep long-lived connections.
[00:03:02] Diego: can you quantify that? like at 120 rps how many concurrent streams are we talking about?
[00:03:08] Ravi: rough calc — with 120 rps and an average response time of 300ms you have about 36 concurrent streams, but if some sessions keep the connection open for multi-turn then that number jumps. that's why we ask for typical session length and KV-cache hit distribution.
[00:03:24] Aisha: session length is typically 3 turns, KV cache reuse about 65% on average. that should help.
[00:03:31] Priya: also curious about fallback behavior — if streaming capacity is saturated do you automatically switch to the non-streaming variant?
[00:03:38] Ravi: yes we can route by policy. for the POC we'll test both policies: sticky streaming for session continuity and a fallback to non-streaming when capacity thresholds hit. we can simulate that with the harness by introducing artificial resource constraints.
[00:03:53] Maeve: let's talk telemetry. Diego, what observability do you need in the POC?
[00:03:59] Diego: we need token-level cost, model version tagging, per-call trace IDs, and structured audit logs with user ids masked. also we'd like to see KV cache hit rates surfaced.
[00:04:12] Ravi: all doable. we'll surface token counts and cost estimates from the harness and include a trace ID in the response headers so your APM can join traces.
[00:04:20] Aisha: on the harness side, our scripts are in python and already emit Prometheus metrics. can we run the Redwood adapter as a sidecar or do we need to push logs to your system?
[00:04:30] Ravi: you can run the harness adapter as a sidecar in your test cluster; we also support pushing to your Prometheus or pulling via scrape targets. sidecar is easiest for an isolated POC.
[00:04:40] Samir: security checks — we are uncomfortable with keys sitting on dev boxes. what's the recommended KMS pattern?
[00:04:46] Maeve: we recommend using customer-managed KMS with envelope encryption. we support HSM-backed keys for Private deployments and we can work with your rotation window. please share KMS policy details.
[00:04:58] Diego: noted, i'll add that as an action.
[00:05:02] Priya: timeline — what does a 3-week POC look like?
[00:05:07] Maeve: typical timeline we propose: week 0 (this week) - onboarding and script handoff; week 1 - baseline non-streaming runs and security/networking checks; week 2 - streaming trials and policy tests + adversarial eval; week 3 - cost tuning and final report. so about 3 calendar weeks.
[00:05:25] Aisha: ok that aligns with our internal window; we have exec check in on 2027-05-24 so deliverable by 2027-05-20 would be ideal.
[00:05:33] Ravi: we'll scope deliverables: raw harness logs + grafana dashboards, a short report with p95/p99 and throughput curves, cost estimate, and recommended config for production.
[00:05:44] Maeve: about benchmarks — what's the key metric matrix we should use?
[00:05:48] Diego: p95 latency, p99 tail, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, and cache hit efficiency. also schedule sensitivity — how performance degrades with bursts.
[00:05:58] Ravi: good. we will create a workload matrix with axes: sequence length (short/medium/long), streaming vs non-streaming, kv-cache hit rates (20/65/90%), and concurrency (low/target/peak). we'll run each cell and sample p95/p99/cost.
[00:06:13] Aisha: you'll need our canonical prompt templates and those adversarial prompts — where should we upload them?
[00:06:18] Maeve: we'll send a shared drive link after the call; please include expected tokenization counts if you have them.
[00:06:25] Samir: one more thing — we have regulatory requirement to keep PHI within region; can Redwood guarantee region pinning during the POC?
[00:06:32] Maeve: for Hosted, we can pin region and ensure data residency for the test. for Dedicated/Private that's even simpler — we'll note this in the security checklist.
[00:06:41] Priya: regarding failure modes, we'd like to see graceful degradation: 429 backpressure responses, circuit-breaker behavior, and a plan if the model variant fails.
[00:06:51] Ravi: we'll include a canary policy and automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant; we'll test the behavior in harness by killing a node mid-run.
[00:06:59] Aisha: perfect. any blockers from Redwood side to start?
[00:07:03] Ravi: we just need the scripts, region, KMS details, and a list of IPs for allowlisting. after that we'll schedule the baseline run.
[00:07:12] Maeve: i'll assign next steps in the follow-up email and sync with pricing to give a dedicated pool estimate.
[00:07:17] Priya: timings — can we get the baseline numbers by 2027-05-10?
[00:07:21] Ravi: yes that's our target.
[00:07:23] Maeve: ok let's open it up for quick clarifying ques — Diego?
[00:07:28] Diego: curious about cost modelling for streaming vs non-streaming — how do you calculate incremental cost? is it tokens only or longer-lived connection charges?
[00:07:36] Ravi: primarily token-based but we also account for instance time for long-lived streams in dedicated deployments. for hosted we'll show effective cost per 1k tokens and an estimated instance overhead for high concurrent streams.
[00:07:48] Aisha: any chance we can run a quick micro-run now, like 100 requests non-streaming, just to sanity check connectivity?
[00:07:55] Ravi: we can, but we'll need your test creds and allowlist first. if you can post those to the shared drive after the call we can attempt a smoke-run tomorrow.
[00:08:04] Aisha: will do.
[00:08:06] Maeve: great, circling back on success criteria — i'll write the candidate success criteria and post it. everyone please confirm or push back by EOD friday.
[00:08:16] Priya: noted.
[00:08:18] Samir: quick note: our batch windows have bursts where tokens spike to 6k; worth validating quantization options for those long sequences.
[00:08:26] Ravi: yes we'll include quantization and memory footprint checks for long sequences in the matrix.
[00:08:33] Aisha: thanks everyone, useful call.
[00:08:36] Maeve: thanks all. we'll follow up with the onboarding pack and a calendar invite for the dry-run.
[00:08:42] (crosstalk/closes)

End of transcript.
